subject: Embedded session sampling variance and requested billing evidence
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmetech.eu>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Accounts Payable <accounts-payable@acmetech.eu>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00+00:00
Subject: Unexpected embed/session charges on Nov 21 invoice

Hi Lauren,

Our Nov 21 invoice shows a ~38% jump in "embed-session" units vs prior weeks (line item: embed-session.v2). We run nightly batch indexing that shouldn't change — no deploys or traffic spikes on our side. Can you help explain the delta before we process payment?

We pulled a sample of tokens from our end and the counts don't line up with the CSV attached (usage_export_20261121.csv). If you can provide the server-side sampling window or tokenization snapshots for Nov 21 (UTC), that'd be great.

Also flagging VAT treatment — we're in the Netherlands and need to confirm reverse-charge placement for that invoice.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Head of Finance, Acme Tech
attachments: usage_export_20261121.csv
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmetech.eu>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T14:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected embed/session charges on Nov 21 invoice

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and attaching your CSV. Sorry for the noise here. I'm looping in Ben (billing + usage) and Marissa (customer success) to dig into the logs and VAT placement.

Quick plan:
- Ben, can you pull the tokenization/sampling snapshots and the prefix-caching window for Acme's tenant for Nov 20-22 (UTC)? Samir attached their sample; we should reconcile to our server-side sampling.
- Marissa, please check any rate-plan changes on Nov 15–21 and confirm whether any auxiliary model routing or fallback (we saw a brief aux-model redirect on Nov 21 at ~02:47 UTC) could explain higher unit accounting.

Samir — we'll aim to return a reconstruction + proposed credit (if warranted) within 5 business days. For VAT, we'll confirm reverse-charge eligibility once we validate the final billed units.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmetech.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:22:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected embed/session charges on Nov 21 invoice — token trace attached

Hi all,

I've pulled the server-side evidence and attached the token trace (redwood_token_trace_20261121.jsonl). Summary of findings:

1) Sampling window mismatch — Acme's client-side exporter and our billing window were misaligned by 30 minutes on Nov 21 due to daylight-saving / UTC conversion in their ingest pipeline. Their exporter truncated late-night batches to the previous day; our server attributed those late-night requests to Nov 21 UTC. The result: apparent duplication when you compared your CSV to our usage export.

2) Aux-model fallback — at 02:47:33 UTC we had a temporary routing fallback to an auxiliary reranker for ~4 minutes. The reranker has a higher per-request unit multiplier for embed-session.v2 (it doesn't use KV cache). This produced an incremental ~2.6% unit increase for that 4-minute window.

3) Prefix cache eviction — during a high-concurrency burst the tenant's prefix cache warmed differently than historical patterns, increasing effective tokenization calls per session by a small amount (~1.7% across the day).

Combined, these explain ~36-38% of the delta you observed. We export the raw per-request token counts in the attached JSONL for audit.

Action items:
- We'll issue a provisional credit for the 30-minute overlap allocation where duplication occurred (pro-rata) pending your confirmation.
- Marissa: please confirm the credit amount and we can issue as an invoice-adj credit.
- Samir: if you can confirm your internal timezone used in the exporter (including any DST offsets) I'll re-run attribution and finalize the credit.

Attachments: redwood_token_trace_20261121.jsonl (per-request rows: timestamp, request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, unit_cost_tag)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmetech.eu>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Accounts Payable <accounts-payable@acmetech.eu>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T16:45:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected embed/session charges on Nov 21 invoice — token trace attached

Thanks Ben — that all makes sense and the JSONL lines up with the discrepant rows we flagged. Our exporter was using Europe/Amsterdam local time but did not account for the DST rollback on Oct 31; that explains the 30-minute misalignment.

Please proceed with the provisional pro-rata credit for the duplicated window and mark the invoice as eligible for reverse-charge VAT (we'll supply our VAT ID via secure doc). Two quick asks before we close:

1) Can you add a short note to the credit describing "pro-rata correction for sampling window misalignment (Nov 21 UTC) + aux-model fallback attenuation" — we need that on our AP record.
2) For our engineering team: could Ben or Marissa share a small bullet list of recommended exporter checks (timezone config, batching window, and request_id continuity) so we reduce recurrence?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Samir Khan
Head of Finance, Acme Tech
